I am Alberto Alamia, a psychiatrist and biostatistician ([telepsichiatria.org](https://telepsichiatria.org)).
This site collects methodological reviews of published research in two fields I work in:
psychiatry and animal behaviour. They share the same weak spots, small samples, latent
constructs measured through proxies, mis-specified models, and conclusions that outrun the data.

## Two tracks

**Systematic.** Papers chosen by a stated sampling rule, without prior suspicion, to estimate
how common serious methodological problems are. The rule is in the
[protocol](protocol.qmd#selection).

**Selected.** Papers chosen for their interest, or suggested by colleagues. Same protocol,
different purpose: to comment, not to count.

Well-analysed papers are reviewed too, and said to be so.

## How to read a review

Each concern carries an evidence tag. *Confirmed* means it follows from the paper's own
numbers. *Inferred* means it depends on a reasonable assumption about what was done. *Needs
data* means only the raw data or code can settle it. Re-analyses, when possible, are Bayesian,
written in Stan, with models and data in the repository.

## Right of reply

Authors receive the review before it is posted and their response is published alongside it.
Corrections to my own errors are made in place and logged.

## Contact and suggestions

Suggest a paper or point out an error by opening an
[issue](https://github.com/albertoalamia/articles_reviews/issues) or by email through
telepsichiatria.org.
